course_description:
Topics relating to specific technologies in chemical engineering. For details and availability, contact Head of School.

In 2026 CHEE3008 will run as Industrial Decarbonisation. The course aims to equip students with essential skills in industrial decarbonisation tailored to chemical and manufacturing processes. In response to growing regulatory, commercial, and societal pressures to reduce industrial emissions, this course will enable students to systematically quantify emissions, apply life cycle assessment methods, and design and evaluate decarbonisation strategies for existing plants.

prerequisites: You'll need to complete the following courses before enrolling in this one:

course_aims: This course develops students’ ability to analyse industrial chemical and manufacturing processes to identify energy demands and quantify greenhouse gas emissions across material, energy, and utility systems. Students gain practical skills in emissions accounting, life cycle assessment (LCA), and uncertainty analysis, enabling them to construct and interpret emissions inventories and key performance metrics. The course also focuses on the design and critical evaluation of decarbonisation strategies for existing plants, including process modifications, electrification, efficiency improvements, and carbon capture options. Emphasis is placed on assessing the technical, environmental, and economic implications of these strategies to support informed engineering decision-making.

learning_outcomes.description: Analyse industrial chemical and manufacturing processes to identify and quantify major sources of greenhouse gas emissions across material, energy, and utility systems.
Develop emissions inventories and apply life cycle assessment (LCA) methods to calculate emissions intensities and related environmental performance metrics for industrial processes.
Propose technically feasible decarbonisation strategies for existing industrial plants, drawing on process modifications, technology substitution, electrification, and carbon mitigation options.
Evaluate and compare decarbonisation options by estimating changes in process performance, lifecycle emissions, and capital and operating costs to support evidence based engineering decisions.

assessment_details.title: Interim Report
assessment_details.task_description: The complete project description will be posted to Blackboard in Week 1. The project will focus on the decarbonisation pathways for an industrial facility in Australia. Information about specific facilities in Australia will be provided, although students may propose an alternate facility with justification. Ultimately the decision of whether the alternate facility is permitted will be at the sole discretion of the Course Coordinator. The project will be completed individually. The interim report will focus on establishing the baseline performance and life cycle analysis of the facility. learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 1 To Week 13
learning_activities.topic: Lectures and guest lectures Core lectures delivered by the teaching team will focus on Australian industries, decarbonisation pathways, and tools that help evaluate the various decarbonisation options. These will include industries like alumina, aluminium, cement, fertilisers, fuels, iron / steel, plastics. Decarbonisation pathways will typically follow a hierachy of offsets, fuel switching, electrification, carbon capture and storage, and new process chemistries. Tools will build on existing knowledge but may include life cycle assessment, economic analysis and multi-criteria decision making. Guest lecturers may deliver lectures related to specific industries or pathways depending on availability. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04

learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 1 To Week 13
learning_activities.topic: Workshops and tutorials Tutorials will be focussed on building experience and expertise with the tools, industries and decarbonisation pathways. The problem sets will be the focus of the tutorials and will build skills for both the project and the exam. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04
